chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not be in the 'aykal.' I asked: 'What is the 'aykal?' He said: 'That you pray behind the rows alone. If entering the row is not possible, he stands opposite the Imam and it suffices him. But if he opposes the row, his prayer is invalidated.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْعَيْكَل: The 'aykal', referring to praying behind the rows of the congregation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying alone behind the congregation rows in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the term 'aykal' (praying alone behind the rows) as a specific state of isolation that, when done deliberately against the congregation's order, invalidates the prayer. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on unity and proper alignment in congregational prayer, distinguishing between mere inability to join the row—which is excused—and stubborn refusal to align, which constitutes a defect. This ruling underscores the spiritual and communal significance of following the Imam's lead in physical positioning during Salah.
